title: A heavy harvest
summary: The terraces of your hearth yield beyond what the granary was built to hold, and the carts stand full in the road.

title: A kiln fire
summary: A kiln in your hearth cracks in the night and the fire runs along the drying racks toward the workshops.

title: An ashfall squall
summary: Grey ash comes down on your hearth for three days, thick enough to choke the lanes and dim the lamps at noon.

title: Wandering scholars
summary: A company of wandering scholars asks to lodge the winter in your hearth, offering their records of the Witness Roads in return.

title: A glass tremor
summary: The seam beneath your hearth shudders in the night and a fissure of ashglass opens through the lower terraces.

title: Refugees on the road
summary: A column of people driven out by the war reaches the gate of your hearth, carrying what they could and asking to stay.

title: Tide wrack
summary: A storm tide leaves the shore below your hearth heaped with wrack, drowned timber and the broken hull of a stranger’s boat.

title: An old quarter gives way
summary: A scarred quarter of your hearth that was never properly rebuilt gives way in the rains, and the lane behind it goes with it.

title: A drowned ledger
summary: A coaster founders in the harbor mouth of your hearth and the divers bring up its strongbox and a sodden ledger of every port it called at.

title: The harbor silts
summary: A season of storms has silted the harbor of your hearth until the deeper hulls scrape at low water.

title: Fire in the archive
summary: A lamp falls in the Witness archive of your hearth and the oldest shelves catch before the watch wakes.

title: A visiting Witness
summary: A Witness of the old roads lodges in the archive of your hearth and offers to read its oldest records aloud, for a fee or for a favour.

title: Fever in the garrison
summary: A fever runs through the companies quartered at your hearth, and the surgeons ask for the stores.

title: A veteran’s drill
summary: An old campaigner settled in your hearth offers to drill the companies quartered there through the winter.

title: A vein of ashglass
summary: Quarrymen at your hearth break into a vein of ashglass running off the seam, brittle and bright.

title: A border fair
summary: Traders from beyond the border ask to hold a fair outside the walls of your hearth while the peace holds.

title: A petition from the far hearths
summary: Elders from the realm’s farthest hearths reach your hearth to petition for a share of the stores kept there.

title: The first winter
summary: The first hard winter closes on the new hearth of your hearth before its granary is finished.

title: Pilgrims on the road
summary: A band of pilgrims following the old Witness Roads stops at your hearth and asks only for water and a place to sleep.

title: A wolf winter
summary: Wolves come down to the outlying farms of your hearth in a hard winter and the herders will not go out without an escort.

title: A merchant’s bequest
summary: A merchant of your hearth dies without heirs and leaves the realm the choice of his warehouse or his library.

title: The well is fouled
summary: The great well of your hearth comes up foul and the lower quarters fall sick.

title: A quiet season
summary: The season passes quietly at your hearth: no raiders, no fever, a fair harvest, and the companies idle in the yard.

title: The seam hums
summary: For a week the seam beneath your hearth hums so that the glass in every window sings, and the Waykeepers ask to be left alone with it.

title: Sickness in the lanes
summary: A sickness takes hold in the lower lanes of your hearth, and the surgeons ask for the lanes to be closed before it climbs the hill.

title: The sickness spreads
summary: The sickness climbs the hill of your hearth faster than the surgeons can follow it.

title: The dying season
summary: The dying season closes on your hearth, and the bells do not stop.

title: Riders on the ridge
summary: Riders are seen on the ridge above your hearth, counting its herds and its gates.

title: The riders strike
summary: The riders come down on the farms of your hearth at dawn, and the herds are already moving.

title: The riders driven off
summary: The riders are driven off from your hearth and leave what they took in the ditches along the road.

title: The river rising
summary: The river below your hearth rises a hand a day, and the lower fields are already wet.

title: The levees hold
summary: The levees at your hearth hold, and the flood passes on down the valley to someone else’s fields.

title: The river floods
summary: The river takes the lower fields of your hearth and does not give them back for a season.

title: A dispute at the toll
summary: Carters on the new road through your hearth refuse the toll and block the gate with their wagons until it is settled.

title: Wardens for the road
summary: The carters’ guild of your hearth asks for a company to ward the road for a season, and offers to pay for it.

title: Rumours of glass
summary: Travellers at your hearth swear the Ashfall glass on the ridge sings at night, now that everyone knows what a seam is.

title: Pilgrims to the seam
summary: Pilgrims come to your hearth to see the seam its borders hold, and will not be kept from it.

title: The fever of the bid
summary: Word that a realm has opened its bid for the world reaches your hearth, and the market will talk of nothing else.

title: Wagers on the future
summary: The bookmakers of your hearth are taking wagers on which realm will close the age.

title: Pilgrims at the old place
summary: Pilgrims come up the road to the old place within the borders of your hearth, more each day, and ask leave to camp beside it.

title: Relic hunters
summary: Diggers with a licence from nobody have opened a pit at the old place within the borders of your hearth.

title: The find
summary: The diggers at the old place of your hearth have brought something up: a sealed jar, a sheet of beaten metal, writing nobody here can read.

title: A keeper for the place
summary: An old woman who has lived beside the old place of your hearth longer than anyone remembers asks the hearth for a stipend to keep it.

title: The stones are moved
summary: Somebody has shifted the stones of the old place within the borders of your hearth in the night, and the farmers will not work the fields beside it.

title: A festival at the old place
summary: The people of your hearth ask to hold the summer festival at the old place within its borders, as their grandparents did.

title: The last of the grain
summary: The stores of your hearth are down to the seed grain, and the millers ask whether they are to grind it.

title: A toll at our own gate
summary: The road wardens have set a toll bar at the gate of your hearth itself and will not lift it for the hearth’s own carts.

title: The clerks fall sick
summary: The fever has reached the clerks of your hearth; half the ledgers lie open and no one is well enough to close them.

title: The cistern cracks
summary: A night tremor has cracked the great cistern of your hearth, and the water is running into the lanes.

title: A run on the market
summary: The merchants of your hearth are calling in every debt at once, and the market square is a shouting match.

title: Ash in the fields
summary: Ash is lying on the standing crop of your hearth, and the reeves ask whether to bring it in green or leave it to the dark.

title: A hermit at the old place
summary: A hermit has taken up living at the old place within the borders of your hearth, and the farmers bring him bread and questions.

title: Stone-robbers
summary: Carts have been seen at night at the old place within the borders of your hearth, and the dressed stone is going somewhere.

title: The bare place
summary: The old place of your hearth stands stripped to its footings, and the pilgrims who came for it have stopped coming.

title: A market at the stones
summary: Traders from beyond the border have begun to meet at the old place within the borders of your hearth, and ask the hearth’s leave to make a market of it.

title: Travellers’ tales
summary: A company of travellers lodged at your hearth swears the old place within its borders is spoken of across the sea, and offers to tell what they know for a fee.

title: Fire at the old place
summary: A grass fire has run up to the old place within the borders of your hearth, and the wardens ask whether to fight it there or let it burn to the stones.

title: Seed from the next valley
summary: Carters from beyond the blight offer your hearth clean seed at twice the price, and the reeves ask whether to pay it or sow what the hearth has.

title: Glass in the thatch
summary: The storm has left the roofs of your hearth full of glass, and the thatchers will not go up until they are paid double.

title: The granary doors
summary: A crowd stands at the granary doors of your hearth with the price chalked on a board, and the keeper asks whether to open them.

title: The lantern festival
summary: The lanes of your hearth ask for oil to light every door on the night of the Ashfall’s turning, as the old towns did.

title: The widows’ toll
summary: The widows of the fallen stand at the granary door of your hearth with their children and ask for bread.

title: A harbor-master’s offer
summary: A harbor-master from beyond the sea offers to run the quay of your hearth for a cut of what passes over it.

title: The lost ledger
summary: The clerks of your hearth have found an old tax roll behind a shelf, naming dues nobody has paid in a generation.

title: Muster day
summary: The companies quartered at your hearth ask for a day of games before the campaigning season.

title: The long peace
summary: The smiths of your hearth ask leave to beat the spare spearheads into ploughshares, since no war has come up the roads.

title: Far cousins
summary: Kin from the far hearths of the realm have come to your hearth asking for land of their own.

title: The first harvest
summary: The first crop of your hearth is in, and the hearth asks what is to be done with it.

title: The cistern silts
summary: The great cistern of your hearth is silting, and the water comes up brown.

title: A foundling at the gate
summary: A child has been left at the gate of your hearth with a token nobody can read.

title: A glass pedlar
summary: A pedlar at your hearth opens a pack of ashglass shards he swears came from the seam, and asks a price.

title: Rumours of the bid
summary: The merchants of your hearth are laying wagers on which realm’s bid will carry, and ask whether the hearth will stake with them.

title: The wager comes due
summary: The merchants of your hearth have settled the wager, and the hearth’s stake has come back with more.

title: The tide flats
summary: A spring tide has left the flats below your hearth bare and covered in shellfish.

title: The old walls fall
summary: A stretch of the old wall of your hearth has come down in the night across two lanes.

title: The bell-founders
summary: A company of bell-founders has set up its pit outside your hearth and offers to cast the hearth a bell that will be heard three valleys off.

title: The tax-farmers
summary: A syndicate offers to collect the dues of your hearth for a season, paying the hearth now and keeping whatever more it can wring out.

title: Ash in the wells
summary: The wells of your hearth have come up grey; the ash of the ruined quarter has found the water.

title: A whale ashore
summary: A whale has come ashore below your hearth, and the whole hearth is on the beach with knives and buckets.

title: Lights over the seam
summary: Lights have been seen over the seam near your hearth three nights running, and the lanes will not pass that road after dark.

title: Deserters at the gate
summary: A dozen deserters from the realm’s own companies have come to the gate of your hearth asking to be let in.

title: The customs house
summary: The merchants of your hearth ask that the quay be given a customs house, with clerks to count what lands and take the realm’s due.

title: The customs dues
summary: The customs house of your hearth has counted its first season, and the clerks lay the books before the hearth.

title: Fire in the scriptorium
summary: A lamp has gone over in the scriptorium of your hearth; the copies are saved but the originals are burning.

title: The quartermaster’s count
summary: The quartermaster of the companies at your hearth has counted the rolls against the ration and found them a company short.

title: The peace fair
summary: With the roads quiet, the carters ask your hearth for a fair at the crossroads, three days with the gates open.

title: The border stones
summary: The far farms of your hearth are quarrelling over where the border stones stood before the Ashfall.

title: An early winter
summary: The first winter of your hearth has come early and the herd has no fodder laid in.

title: Old debts called in
summary: With the bids in the air, the moneylenders of your hearth are calling in every old debt of the hearth at once.

title: The glassblowers’ guild
summary: The glassblowers of your hearth ask for a charter of their own, with the right to buy ashglass before the realm does.

title: The horse fair
summary: The horse fair has pitched outside your hearth, and the dealers ask the hearth’s price for the ground.

title: The night watch
summary: The lanes of your hearth ask for a paid night watch after a season of thefts.

title: The scorched orchards
summary: The orchards of your hearth were burned in the troubles, and the growers ask for saplings.

title: Driftwood hulls
summary: A storm has thrown the wrecks of two ships onto the shore below your hearth.

title: The seam chanters
summary: A company of chanters has camped at the seam near your hearth and offers to sing the glass up for a fee.

title: The levy called
summary: The companies at your hearth ask the hearth to raise its levy for the war.

title: Fire on the quay
summary: A tar-pot has gone over on the quay of your hearth and the sheds are alight.

title: A visiting chronicler
summary: A chronicler of another realm asks to read in the archive of your hearth for a season.

title: The barracks brawl
summary: Two companies quartered at your hearth have fought in the lanes, and the lanes want the damages paid.

title: The roads reopened
summary: With the roads at peace, the carters of your hearth ask for coin to mend the far stretches.

title: A distant kin’s summons
summary: A far hearth of the realm has sent to your hearth for grain and coin after a hard season.

title: The stockade
summary: The households of your hearth ask for a stockade before the first raiders find the new hearth.

title: The bidder’s envoy
summary: An envoy of a realm that bids for the age has come to your hearth asking to be heard.

title: The envoy returns
summary: The bidder’s envoy has returned to your hearth with a gift for the hearth that heard the bid.

title: The ash moths
summary: A swarm of ash moths has settled on the fields of your hearth and is eating the standing crop.

title: The salt road toll
summary: The carters on the salt road through your hearth ask whether the hearth means to toll the road now that it is kept.

title: The midwinter feast
summary: The wards of your hearth ask the hearth to pay for the midwinter feast, as it did in better years.

title: The rubble market
summary: Masons from the next valley offer to buy the rubble of the fallen quarter of your hearth.

title: The seal colony
summary: A colony of seals has hauled out on the rocks below your hearth, and the shore folk have their clubs ready.

title: The seam goes cold
summary: The diggers at the seam near your hearth say the glass has gone cold and ask for coin to cut deeper.

title: The wounded column
summary: A column of wounded from the realm’s companies has come to the gate of your hearth asking for beds and bread.

title: The pilots’ dispute
summary: The harbor pilots of your hearth will not bring ships over the bar until their fee is raised.

title: The ledger of the dead
summary: The clerks of your hearth ask leave to compile a ledger of every household lost since the Ashfall.

title: The drill sergeant
summary: An old sergeant of another realm offers to drill the companies quartered at your hearth for a season’s pay.

title: A wedding of houses
summary: Two great houses of your hearth will marry their children, and ask the hearth to stand the dower.

title: The far survey
summary: The clerks of your hearth ask for coin to survey the far holdings of the realm properly.

title: The first well
summary: The households of your hearth carry water from the stream and ask for a well.

title: The glass scare
summary: A rumour runs the lanes of your hearth that the ashglass in the stores is giving the glass sickness.

title: Rival envoys
summary: Envoys of two realms that bid for the age have come to your hearth in the same week, each asking the hearth to carry its word.

title: The counter-envoy returns
summary: The envoy of your hearth has returned from the bidding courts with terms and letters.

title: The hearth census
summary: The clerks of your hearth ask to count the households door by door, as the rolls have not been read since the Ashfall.

title: The ale shortage
summary: The brewers of your hearth cannot keep up with the wards, and the taverns are watering what they pour.

title: Squatters in the ruins
summary: Landless folk have moved into the burnt quarter of your hearth and are roofing the shells with thatch.

title: The kelp harvest
summary: The storms have heaped the shore below your hearth with kelp, and the shore folk ask for carts to bring it up for the fields.

title: Fumes from the seam
summary: The diggers at the seam near your hearth come up sick from fumes in the cut.

title: The smiths pressed
summary: The realm’s quartermasters want every smith in your hearth forging for the companies until the war is done.

title: The harbor light
summary: The keeper of the harbor light at your hearth has died, and no one has tended the flame for a week.

title: The borrowed books
summary: A scholar of another realm asks to borrow from the archive of your hearth and promises copies in return.

title: The garrison wedding
summary: A captain quartered at your hearth will marry into the hearth, and the companies ask a feast of the hall.

title: The market charter
summary: With no war on the roads, the merchants of your hearth ask a charter to hold the market twice a week.

title: The far tithe
summary: The far holdings of the realm send their tithe to your hearth late and short, with a letter of excuses.

title: The first orchard
summary: The households of your hearth ask for saplings to set the first orchard on the slope above the fields.

title: The glass tithe
summary: Priests of the seam ask your hearth for a tithe of its ashglass for the shrine they are raising.

title: The bidder’s wager
summary: An agent of a realm that bids for the age offers your hearth coin to lay a wager on its bid, the stake to be settled when the bid is read.

title: The wager settled
summary: The agent has come back to your hearth to settle the wager, and the stake is more than the coin was.

title: The road menders
summary: The carters ask your hearth to mend the road out of the gate, where the ruts have broken two axles this month.

title: The wards’ quarrel
summary: Two wards of your hearth quarrel over the well between them, and the watch has twice broken up a fight at it.

title: The salvage rights
summary: Salvagers ask your hearth for the right to pick the fallen quarter for its timber and iron.

title: The shipwreck’s cargo
summary: A wreck’s cargo has washed up on the shore below your hearth: casks, bales and a strongbox.

title: The seam cartel
summary: Glass merchants offer your hearth a price for everything the seam gives this year, paid now.

title: The war levy
summary: The realm’s marshal asks your hearth for a levy of its young men to fill the companies.

title: The harbor dredging
summary: The channel into the harbor of your hearth has silted until the deep hulls wait outside the bar.

title: The copyists’ strike
summary: The copyists of the archive of your hearth have put down their pens until their pay is raised.

title: The garrison duel
summary: Two captains quartered at your hearth mean to fight a duel at dawn, and their companies are taking sides.

title: The bridge toll
summary: The bridge-wardens of your hearth ask to toll the bridge now that the roads are safe enough to be busy.

title: The far wedding
summary: A far holding of the realm asks your hearth to send gifts and a witness to its wedding.

title: The first mill
summary: The households of your hearth grind their grain by hand and ask for a mill on the stream.

title: The glass lanterns
summary: Lantern-makers ask your hearth for ashglass from its stores to make seam-lanterns for the lanes.

title: The bidder’s bribe
summary: An agent of a realm that bids for the age offers the clerks of your hearth coin for a sight of the realm’s letters.
